segments.t: Paul, looking steadfastly at the council, said,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: “Brothers,
I have lived before God
in all good conscience
until today.”
The high priest, Ananias,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: commanded those who stood by him
to strike him on the mouth.
Then Paul said to him,
“God will strike you,
you whitewashed wall!
Do you sit to judge me according to the law,
and command me to be struck contrary to the law?”
segments.note: 「contrary to the law」は παρανομῶν の表現

segments.t: Those who stood by said,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: “Do you malign God’s high priest?”
Paul said,
“I didn’t know,
brothers,
that he was high priest.
For it is written,
‘You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.’”
But when Paul perceived
that the one part were Sadducees
and the other Pharisees,
he cried out in the council,
“Men and brothers,
I am a Pharisee,
a son of Pharisees.
Concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged!”
When he had said this,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: an argument arose between the Pharisees and Sadducees,
and the crowd was divided.
For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit;
but the Pharisees confess all of these.
A great clamor arose,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: and some of the scribes of the Pharisees’ part stood up, and contended, saying,
“We find no evil in this man.
But if a spirit or angel has spoken to him,
let’s not fight against God!”
segments.note: WEB はビザンティン本文に従い μὴ θεομαχῶμεν（神に逆らうのはやめよう）を補う。ギリシャ語本文にこの句はない

segments.t: When a great argument arose,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: the commanding officer, fearing that Paul would be torn in pieces by them,
segments.note: 「torn in pieces」は διασπασθῇ の表現

segments.t: commanded the soldiers to go down
and take him by force from among them
segments.note: 「by force」は ἁρπάσαι の表現

segments.t: and bring him into the barracks.
The following night,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: the Lord stood by him and said,
“Cheer up,
Paul,
segments.note: 呼びかけの「Paul」はギリシャ語本文になく、英訳が補ったもの

segments.t: for as you have testified about me at Jerusalem,
so you must testify also at Rome.”
When it was day,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: some of the Jews banded together
and bound themselves under a curse,
saying that they would neither eat nor drink
until they had killed Paul.
There were more than forty people who had made this conspiracy.
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: They came to the chief priests and the elders,
and said,
“We have bound ourselves under a great curse
to taste nothing
until we have killed Paul.
Now therefore,
you with the council inform the commanding officer
that he should bring him down to you
tomorrow,
segments.note: WEB はビザンティン本文に従い αὔριον（明日）を補う。ギリシャ語本文にこの語はない

segments.t: as though you were going to judge his case more exactly.
We are ready to kill him
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: before he comes near.”
But Paul’s sister’s son
heard they were lying in wait,
and he came and entered into the barracks
and told Paul.
Paul summoned one of the centurions and said,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: “Bring this young man to the commanding officer,
for he has something to tell him.”
So he took him and brought him to the commanding officer and said,
“Paul, the prisoner, summoned me and asked me
to bring this young man to you.
He has something to tell you.”
The commanding officer took him by the hand,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: and going aside, asked him privately,
“What is it that you have to tell me?”
He said,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: “The Jews have agreed to ask you
to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow,
as though intending to inquire somewhat more accurately concerning him.
Therefore don’t yield to them,
for more than forty men lie in wait for him,
who have bound themselves under a curse to
neither eat nor drink
until they have killed him.
Now they are ready, looking for the promise from you.”
So the commanding officer let the young man go,
charging him, “Tell no one that you have revealed these things to me.”
He called to himself two of the centurions, and said,
“Prepare two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea,
with seventy horsemen and two hundred men armed with spears,
segments.note: 「men armed with spears」は δεξιολάβους の訳

segments.t: at the third hour of the night.”
He asked them to provide mounts,
that they might set Paul on one,
and bring him safely to Felix the governor.
He wrote a letter like this:
“Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix:
Greetings.
“This man was seized by the Jews,
and was about to be killed by them
when I came with the soldiers and rescued him,
having learned that he was a Roman.
Desiring to know the cause why they accused him,
I brought him down to their council.
I found him to be accused about questions of their law,
but not to be charged with anything worthy of death or of imprisonment.
When I was told that the Jews lay in wait for the man,
segments.note: 「the Jews」は主語の補い。δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: I sent him to you immediately,
charging his accusers also to bring their accusations against him before you.
Farewell.”
segments.note: WEB はビザンティン本文に従い結びの挨拶 Ἔρρωσο（さらば）を補う。ギリシャ語本文にこの語はない

segments.t: So the soldiers, carrying out their orders,
took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.
But on the next day
they left the horsemen to go with him,
and returned to the barracks.
When they came to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor,
they also presented Paul to him.
When the governor had read it,
segments.note: 主語「the governor」は補い。δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: he asked what province he was from.
When he understood that he was from Cilicia,
he said,
segments.note: 「he said」は次節の ἔφη を先取りしたもので、この節のギリシャ語には対応がない

segments.t: “I will hear you fully
when your accusers also arrive.”
He commanded that he be kept in Herod’s palace.
